portInfo.description: On Corsica’s northwest coast, Calvi combines a fortified headland with a marina and a long bay beach. You can have a satisfying day without leaving town:the upper streets provide the historical setting, and the lower waterfront is the easier alternative for anyone avoiding the climb. The Balagne villages are a separate road excursion, not places to append casually to a short tender window.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Calvi — cruise anchorage — n/a — anchorage position allocated per vessel
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The Corsica Cruise Club’s French page explicitly says anchorage only. Secondary Whatsinport identifies Quai Landry as the tender landing; the primary page does not name that quay. Plan on the line’s confirmed marina landing, not an independently chosen yacht pontoon. Allow 45 minutes outward for queue/boat/landing and at least 90 minutes at the end for landing queue, tender and aboard margin; increase this for a more distant anchorage. From Quai Landry, allow 20–30 minutes uphill to the citadel at an unhurried pace. Prearrange any village excursion return to the same landing.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Citadel of Calvi, Citadel entrance, Calvi upper town: Follow the ramparts and cobbled lanes for a compact introduction to the fortified town. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Uphill and uneven; do not describe it as step-free.

Saint-Jean-Baptiste Cathedral, Saint-Jean-Baptiste Cathedral, inside Calvi citadel: A distinct interior stop within the citadel route. Allow about 30 minutes (editorial estimate). Worship/access times unverified; exterior remains a fallback.

Calvi beach, Town end of Calvi beach beside the marina, Calvi: Use the near end of the bay for a manageable beach day. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). No guarantee of lifeguards, swimming or accessible sand routes.

Calvi marina waterfront, Quai Landry/Calvi marina waterfront, Calvi: A flatter café-and-harbour alternative to the citadel climb. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Working marina edges are not unrestricted boarding pontoons.

Paoli Square, Île-Rousse, Place Paoli, Île-Rousse, Balagne: A specific town-centre destination for a longer prearranged road excursion. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). A separate town; allow a full return road block, not a short walk from Calvi.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Photograph the actual tender pickup before climbing. Returning to a different stretch of a yacht harbour can waste the very margin meant to protect the ship connection.
